candidates.title: OS command injection via unsanitized request parameter in shell=True Popen
candidates.rationale: request.args.get('target') flows directly into a concatenated shell command string passed to subprocess.Popen with shell=True. Any attacker who can reach this route controls the shell line, e.g. ?target=127.0.0.1;id, yielding arbitrary command execution as the app's user.
candidates.evidence:
target = request.args.get("target", "")
    return subprocess.Popen("ping -c 1 " + target, shell=True)

candidates.title: Unsafe deserialization of raw request body with pickle.loads
candidates.rationale: request.get_data() is passed straight to pickle.loads. Pickle can invoke arbitrary callables during unpickling, so a crafted body achieves remote code execution before any validation is possible. There is no allowlist, signing, or type check.

candidates.title: SQL injection through string concatenation in cursor.execute
candidates.rationale: The 'name' query parameter is concatenated into the SQL text instead of being bound as a parameter. A value such as ' OR '1'='1 or ' UNION SELECT ... breaks out of the string literal and alters the query, enabling data disclosure and authentication bypass.
candidates.evidence:
name = request.args.get("name", "")
    cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'" )

candidates.title: Unsafe YAML deserialization using yaml.Loader on request body
candidates.rationale: yaml.load with the full yaml.Loader constructor resolves arbitrary Python object tags (e.g. !!python/object/apply:os.system), so attacker-supplied YAML in the request body leads to code execution. yaml.safe_load is the correct call here.
